claims.text: Refractory high-entropy alloys such as MoNbTaW are high-melting materials with a BCC crystalline structure.
A machine-learning interatomic potential can be constructed for MoNbTaW using DFT data from Nb-Ta-Mo-W elemental, binary, ternary, and quaternary systems.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials can achieve accuracy near that of their underlying DFT calculations.
The MoNbTaW moment tensor potential offers a favorable balance between accuracy and computational cost.
A machine-learning-enhanced two-phase coexistence simulation can reproduce melting temperatures with nearly DFT-level accuracy.
A machine-learning-enhanced two-phase coexistence simulation can reproduce fusion entropy and enthalpy with nearly DFT-level accuracy.
A machine-learning-enhanced two-phase coexistence simulation can reproduce the volume change at melting with nearly DFT-level accuracy.
The proposed method requires only a fraction of the computational cost of full DFT thermodynamic integration.
A controlled temperature ramp near melting under fixed pressure or fixed volume ensures thermodynamic equilibrium between solid and liquid regions.
The dynamics and equilibrium position of the solid-liquid interface mediate determination of the melting properties.
Direct simulation of solid-liquid coexistence identifies the melting temperature from the equilibrium coexistence state.
Analysis of energy changes across the solid-liquid interface enables calculation of the enthalpy of fusion.
Analysis of coexistence energetics enables calculation of the entropy of fusion.
Analysis of volume changes across the interface enables calculation of the volume change at melting.
Two-phase coexistence simulations bypass the extensive thermodynamic integration over incremental states used in standard ab initio free-energy methods.
The predicted melting properties will closely match results from full ab initio free-energy integration.
The reduction in computational cost will enable high-throughput screening of refractory materials.
Accuracy may deteriorate for complex microstructures or when the machine-learning potential lacks training data for extreme conditions.
Inaccurate treatment of interface effects or phase-boundary kinetics may cause deviations in predicted melting properties.
The transferability and precision of the machine-learning potential across diverse high-temperature regimes have not been fully validated.
